fields.aka: Dvija Haridāsa, Dvija Haridāsācārya, Baḍa Haridāsa, Haridāsa Dvija
fields.notes:
Son of Nṛsiṁha Mukhuṭī, of the brāhmaṇa-kula; a branch of Lord Caitanya: «Śrī Candraśekhara Vaidya, Dvija Haridāsa» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.112). After the Lord's disappearance he wanted to give up his life; the Lord stopped him in a dream and sent him to Vṛndāvana, where he lived as a renunciant. In Vṛndāvana he asked Śrīnivāsa Ācārya to initiate his two sons, Śrīdāsa and Gokulānanda (Bhakti-ratnākara 6.326-327); he passed away on Māgha Kṛṣṇa Ekādaśī soon after Śrīnivāsa left for Gauḍa, and at the festival for him at Kāñcanagaḍiyā Śrīnivāsa initiated the two sons. Their descendants live at Ṭeñā and Sāṭui. The «Śrī Kṛṣṇa-caitanya-sahasra-nāma», from his talks with Narahari Sarakāra, was made known by Lokānandācārya (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa Ācārya»). Bimanbihari Majumdar also counts him among the devotees of Orissa (Vaiṣṇava-vandanā).

Sons: Śrīdāsa and Gokulānanda (Gokula dāsa), disciples of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya.
